entities.name: National Museum of History
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The National Museum of History of China in Beijing (Zhongguo Guojia Bowuguan), reopened in its current form in 2011 after a massive renovation and expansion, is the largest history museum in the world by exhibition area (approximately 200,000 square meters) and holds over 1.4 million artifacts documenting 5,000 years of Chinese civilization — including the Simuwu Rectangular Ding (the world's largest bronze vessel, c. 1300 BCE), the Houmuwu Ding, and extraordinary collections from every dynasty from Shang through Qing. The museum occupies the eastern side of Tiananmen Square, directly facing the Great Hall of the People.

The museum's location on Tiananmen Square (opposite the Great Hall of the People, flanking the Monument to the People's Heroes) is politically deliberate: it frames Chinese Communist Party governance within the narrative of 5,000 years of continuous Chinese civilization. The museum merged two previous institutions — the Museum of Chinese History and the Museum of the Chinese Revolution (1949-) — in 2003, combining dynastic history with CCP revolutionary history in a single national narrative.

The Simuwu Rectangular Ding (also called Houmuwu Ding) — a massive bronze ritual vessel cast c. 1300 BCE during the Shang dynasty, weighing 832.84 kg and measuring 133 cm tall — is the world's largest known ancient bronze casting and the museum's most important artifact. It was discovered by farmers in 1939, hidden from Japanese occupiers during WWII, and acquired by the National Museum. Annual attendance exceeds 7 million, making it among the world's most visited museums.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The National Museum of History of China — world's largest history museum, on Tiananmen Square, holding 1.4 million artifacts from 5,000 years — is the most politically and culturally loaded national history institution on Earth, deliberately framing the CCP's 75-year rule within the narrative of one of humanity's oldest continuous civilizations.
